article_title: Navigating AI's educational future: expert scenarios and implications for teaching and teacher preparation
citation: Malyn-Smith, J., Torrington, J., Webb, M., Butler, D., Lee, J., Tiernan, P., Chtouki, Y., Bower, M., Yazbak Abu Ahmad, M., Carvalho, A. A., Cohen, J. D., Gorissen, P., Linden, T., MacCallum, K., Raffagheli, J. E., Røkenes, F. M., Ronci, M., Shelton, C., Smith, D., & Vartiainen, H. (2026). Navigating AI's educational future: expert scenarios and implications for teaching and teacher preparation. Computers and Education Open. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.caeo.2026.100422
title: Human-AI collaborative thematic analysis process guided by the IAVES framework
description: The study adapted Braun and Clarke's six-phase reflexive thematic analysis to incorporate systematic human-AI collaboration guided by the IAVES framework for Human-Centered AI Interaction. Multiple GenAI models were used strategically: "AI functioned instrumentally during systematic coding activities, as well as worked as an intellectual partner during interpretive theme development". Nine AI-proposed candidate themes were refined into twelve final themes through human disaggregation, with human researchers retaining full interpretive authority at all decision gates and cross-validation across models functioning as triangulation.
requirements: Human researchers retain interpretive authority and subject AI contributions to the same validation standards expected of human analytical work
constraints: The authors acknowledge that the internal reasoning processes of large language models are not transparent and the basis on which patterns are identified or weighted cannot be fully audited
target_learning_goals: conducting rigorous human-AI collaborative qualitative analysis
examples: ChatGPT-5.1 was used for coding and initial theme generation and Claude 4.5 Sonnet for theme interrogation and argumentation analysis via an auto-interview technique.

article_title: Automaticity of word recognition is a unique predictor of reading fluency in middle-school students.
citation: Roembke Tanja C., Hazeltine Eliot, Reed Deborah K., McMurray Bob. (2019). Automaticity of Word Recognition is a Unique Predictor of Reading Fluency in Middle-School Students. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000279
title: iASK backward-masking experimental tasks (Find the Picture, Find the Rhyme, Verify)
description: The iASK (Iowa Assessment of Skills and Knowledge for reading) development version delivered three computer-based tasks over the Internet: Find the Picture (word-to-picture matching, four options), Find the Rhyme (rhyme selection from eight options), and Verify (auditory-visual match judgment). Each had masked (90 msec, eight hashtags) and unmasked versions. The article reports "experimental tasks showed excellent internal consistency" with Cronbach's alpha ranging from 0.90 to 0.98 across versions. Items were monosyllabic, balanced across GPC classes, with counterbalanced masking assignment.
requirements: Audio instructions and experimenter presence during sessions
constraints: Absolute performance cannot be compared across tasks due to different numbers of response options and chance rates
Find the Picture had more missed trials (mean = 49/60) than other task versions
examples: Participants completed 600 study-relevant trials over four days, approximately 345 trials per day, within a larger interleaved program
key_sources: Roembke Tanja C., Hazeltine Eliot, Reed Deborah K., McMurray Bob. (2019). Automaticity of Word Recognition is a Unique Predictor of Reading Fluency in Middle-School Students. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000279

article_title: How does collaborative task design shape collaborative knowledge construction and group-level regulation of learning? A study of secondary school students’ interactions in two varied tasks
citation: Zabolotna, K., Nøhr, L., Iwata, M., Spikol, D., Malmberg, J., & Järvenoja, H. (2025). How does collaborative task design shape collaborative knowledge construction and group-level regulation of learning? A study of secondary school students' interactions in two varied tasks. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-024-09442-3
title: Gunawardena et al.'s Interaction Analysis Model (IAM) conceptualizing CKC as five phases from pooling of knowledge to agreement
description: The IAM describes CKC as evolving "from lower mental functions, i.e., 'pooling of knowledge,' to higher mental functions through five distinct CKC phases": (1) sharing and comparing information, (2) discovering and exploring dissonance or disagreement, (3) negotiating shared meaning or co-constructing knowledge, (4) testing the proposed synthesis, and (5) reaching agreement expressed through metacognitive statements indicating cognitive change. The study adopts it because it is grounded in social constructivism, has been empirically validated for video-recorded interactions, and captures CKC through interactions with both peers and artifacts. The authors adapted category descriptions to secondary school interactions and excluded the 'agree' phase due to low frequency.
requirements: Video-recorded collaborative interactions amenable to coding of mutually exclusive CKC phases within utterances
constraints: The 'agree' phase was excluded from modeling due to low frequency in these data
target_learners: Secondary school students (eighth and ninth grade)
target_learning_goals: Collaborative knowledge construction in science and robotics tasks
examples: CKC phases coded in video data from the SimSketch drawing task and the Simua robot-building task, with intercoder reliability κ = 0.82 and κ = 0.73 respectively
key_sources: Zabolotna, K., Nøhr, L., Iwata, M., Spikol, D., Malmberg, J., & Järvenoja, H. (2025). How does collaborative task design shape collaborative knowledge construction and group-level regulation of learning? A study of secondary school students' interactions in two varied tasks. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-024-09442-3

article_title: A scoping review of internet addiction and academic performance among health sciences students.
citation: Baghcheghi Nayereh; Koohestani Hamid Reza. (2026). A scoping review of internet addiction and academic performance among health sciences students. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-026-04883-x
title: Indirect-pathway model: internet addiction affects academic performance primarily through mediators rather than direct GPA effects
description: The review proposes that internet addiction's effect on academic performance is "complex, multifaceted, and predominantly indirect," exerted through intermediary factors rather than grade-based indicators. Key mediators named are mental health variables (depression and anxiety), academic burnout, sleep disruption, and surface learning approaches, which "may impair cognitive functioning and academic engagement." A proposed self-care pathway holds that late-night internet use reduces sleep, excessive online time erodes structured routines, and sedentary screen use displaces physical activity. A self-escape model explains the GPA paradox as deteriorating mental health and learning quality rather than direct effects.
requirements: Longitudinal mediation studies to test the directionality of the proposed pathways, as the article states the model requires such testing
constraints: Due to the predominance of cross-sectional designs, the variables should be interpreted as correlates and potential pathways rather than confirmed causal mechanisms
target_learners: Health sciences students in higher education (medicine, dentistry, nursing, pharmacy, allied health)
target_learning_goals: Academic performance (GPA, examination results) and quality of learning processes (learning approaches, engagement, burnout)
examples: The review interprets Colombian, Turkish, Egyptian, and Iranian null GPA findings alongside negative findings from Bangladesh, Pakistan, Egypt/Saudi, and Iran as support for mediated rather than direct effects
key_sources: Baghcheghi Nayereh; Koohestani Hamid Reza. (2026). A scoping review of internet addiction and academic performance among health sciences students. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-026-04883-x

article_title: Efficacy of an Imaging Anatomy Virtual Simulation Experiment Course in Undergraduate Medical Education: Nonrandomized Controlled Trial.
citation: Li A, Ma L, Peng R, Shi J, Zhang M, Zheng M, Wang Y, Huang Y, Ren J. (2026). Efficacy of an Imaging Anatomy Virtual Simulation Experiment Course in Undergraduate Medical Education: Nonrandomized Controlled Trial. JMIR Medical Education. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13171472/
title: Imaging Anatomy Virtual Simulation Experiment (IAVSE) course
description: The IAVSE course is a VR-based anatomy elective built in Unity with Vuforia model-target tracking for Meta Quest 2 headsets, letting students "grab, rotate, and translate the model" and toggle anatomical layers via progressive disclosure. It uses deidentified thin-section CT/MRI data reconstructed into 3D models, links 3D anatomy to 2D tomographic images, and includes gamified jigsaw puzzles and formative checks. It replaced 16 of 40 laboratory hours for the experimental group.
requirements: Meta Quest 2 hardware with inside-out 6-degree-of-freedom tracking; model targets meeting quantitative metrics such as a Vuforia star rating of at least 3 stars and a key point matching rate above 80%
Staggered group training protocol when headset availability is limited, as only 10 units were available
constraints: Development involves notable technical complexity and initial financial investment, which the authors state remained significant barriers to widespread adoption
target_learners: third-year undergraduate medical students in an 8-year clinical medicine program
target_learning_goals: human anatomy (3D structure and spatial relationships) and 2D sectional imaging anatomy relevant to medical imaging
examples: The experimental group completed 24 hours of cadaver-based laboratory plus 16 hours of IAVSE delivered over 7 to 8 weeks with 2 to 3 training hours per week
key_sources: Li A, Ma L, Peng R, Shi J, Zhang M, Zheng M, Wang Y, Huang Y, Ren J. (2026). Efficacy of an Imaging Anatomy Virtual Simulation Experiment Course in Undergraduate Medical Education: Nonrandomized Controlled Trial. JMIR Medical Education. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13171472/

article_title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of dental residents in managing traumatic dental injuries.
citation: Yu Jian, Yu Jingjing, Liu Chang. (2025). Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of dental residents in managing traumatic dental injuries. BMC Oral Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12903-025-07382-4
title: IADT-based TDI questionnaire validated by Delphi expert consultation
description: A structured electronic questionnaire assessing TDI management was developed based on the 2020 IADT guidelines and validated through a Delphi expert consultation. It comprises demographics plus four sections: "Section I evaluated TDI clinical exposure and educational experiences", Section II knowledge competency (five items), Section III professional attitudes (six Likert-scale items), and Section IV clinical practice patterns (four items). It was administered via SoJump and WeChat with digital informed consent.
requirements: Content validity confirmed through three Delphi evaluation rounds by experts with over 10 years of clinical and research experience
constraints: As a heterogeneous knowledge test covering multiple domains, high internal consistency is not theoretically expected, per the authors
target_learners: Dental residents in standardized residency training
target_learning_goals: Assessing knowledge, attitudes, and practices in traumatic dental injury management
examples: Distributed to all 465 eligible residents at Wuhan University with 256 respondents (55.1% response rate), analyzed with descriptive statistics and chi-square tests.
key_sources: Yu Jian, Yu Jingjing, Liu Chang. (2025). Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of dental residents in managing traumatic dental injuries. BMC Oral Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12903-025-07382-4

article_title: Instrumento para Avaliação Formativa em Estágio Supervisionado de Enfermagem®: elaboration and validity.
citation: Ramos Tierle Kosloski; Cogo Silvana Bastos; Nietsche Elisabeta Albertina; Salbego Cléton; Backes Vania Marli Schubert; Adamy Edlamar Kátia; Freitas Etiane de Oliveira; Baixinho Cristina Lavareda. (2025). Instrumento para Avaliação Formativa em Estágio Supervisionado de Enfermagem®: elaboration and validity. Revista Brasileira de Enfermagem. https://doi.org/10.1590/0034-7167-2025-0004
title: IAFEE-ECS® formative assessment instrument for nursing supervised curricular internship
description: IAFEE-ECS® is a validated formative assessment instrument for nursing students in supervised curricular internship (SCI), developed from an integrative literature review, official documents from the Ministry of Education, Federal Nursing Council and Brazilian Nursing Association, and Philippe Perrenoud's theoretical framework. It contains identification information, usage guidelines, four domains, 27 items, descriptive assessment by professors and supervisors, and student self-assessment. Evaluators assign scores from 0 to 10 per item, with domain sums divided by item count to yield formative assessment results, and the arithmetic mean of two formative assessments producing the final summative grade.
requirements: Used by professors, supervising nurses and students, enabling self-assessment throughout the internship period
constraints: Validated only with experts from public HEIs in nursing, not including private institutions
target_learners: Nursing students in supervised curricular internship
target_learning_goals: Education, investigation/research in nursing and health

article_title: Instrumento para Avaliação Formativa em Estágio Supervisionado de Enfermagem®: elaboration and validity.
citation: Ramos Tierle Kosloski; Cogo Silvana Bastos; Nietsche Elisabeta Albertina; Salbego Cléton; Backes Vania Marli Schubert; Adamy Edlamar Kátia; Freitas Etiane de Oliveira; Baixinho Cristina Lavareda. (2025). Instrumento para Avaliação Formativa em Estágio Supervisionado de Enfermagem®: elaboration and validity. Revista Brasileira de Enfermagem. https://doi.org/10.1590/0034-7167-2025-0004
title: Four-domain structure with descriptive reports and self-assessment fields per domain
description: The instrument's first version comprised five assessment chunks: a header with identification data, presentation and usage guidelines, four domains with their items (transversal skills; nursing care; nursing management; education and research), space below each domain for "the evaluator and the student to write a descriptive report, aiming at their self-assessment", and a formula for the final formative assessment. Scores of 0 to 10 are assigned per item, and the summative grade is the simple arithmetic mean of the two formative assessments.
requirements: Guidelines for use must accompany the instrument
Fields for self-assessment and observations/comments must be present
target_learners: Nursing students in supervised curricular internship
target_learning_goals: Holistic assessment of clinical competency across four professional domains
key_sources: Ramos Tierle Kosloski; Cogo Silvana Bastos; Nietsche Elisabeta Albertina; Salbego Cléton; Backes Vania Marli Schubert; Adamy Edlamar Kátia; Freitas Etiane de Oliveira; Baixinho Cristina Lavareda. article_title: Contribution of simulation in paediatric laparoscopic surgery: improving suturing skills before performing a laparoscopic procedure in children.
citation: Bidault-Jourdainne Valeska, Breaud Jean, Ali Liza, Talon Isabelle, Becmeur François, Ghoneimi Alaa El, Peycelon Matthieu. (2024). Contribution of simulation in paediatric laparoscopic surgery: improving suturing skills before performing a laparoscopic procedure in children. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06346-6
title: IAD_PLSC practical simulation training program
description: The inter-academic paediatric laparoscopic surgery degree (IAD_PLSC) is a French nation-wide training program combining theoretical training by experts with mentored practical training on pelvitrainers. Its "structure of practical simulation training over two one-week sessions of 12 h each, five months apart" is described as corresponding to deliberate practice. Trainees work in pairs alternating training and observation every 15 minutes, practice intracorporeal laparoscopic knots with 5-mm and 3-mm instruments, and are assessed with an adapted OSATS score out of 40 plus knot completion time.
requirements: Supervision by consultants with a minimum of four-year experience in laparoscopic surgery and in simulation
Trainees attend the practical afternoons and the final practical evaluation (absence from more than two afternoons was an exclusion criterion)
constraints: The study evaluated it retrospectively, without a control group of trainees with only theoretical and video learning
Only one adult-size pelvi-trainer box and one length of 3-mm instruments were offered
target_learners: residents in paediatric surgery and paediatric urology
target_learning_goals: intracorporeal laparoscopic knot tying and suturing skills
basic laparoscopic skills (peg transfer, cord manipulation, pattern cutting)
examples: In 2021 and 2022, 43 trainees completed the program (25 in 2021, 18 in 2022); 28 (65%) had followed programs outside Europe with no access to PLSC training
key_sources: Bidault-Jourdainne Valeska, Breaud Jean, Ali Liza, Talon Isabelle, Becmeur François, Ghoneimi Alaa El, Peycelon Matthieu. (2024). Contribution of simulation in paediatric laparoscopic surgery: improving suturing skills before performing a laparoscopic procedure in children. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06346-6
